senses.gloss:
जर जर, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. जॄ), becoming
old or worn out, old; wearing out; causing old age,
producing decay, consuming; (अस्), m. wearing out,
wasting; (आ), f. the becoming old, old age; old age
personified as a daughter of Death; decrepitude, the
general debility consequent upon old age; digestion;
a kind of date tree, = क्षीरिका; N. of a Rākṣasī
worshipped for having united the two halves into
which Jarā-sandha (q. v.) was divided at his birth;
[cf. वि-जर.]
—जरातुर (˚रा-आत्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, in-
firm, decrepit, debilitated, old.
—जरा-परिणत,
अस्, आ, अम्, stooping, bent down with age or infirmity.
—जरा-पुष्ट, अस्, m. = जरा-सन्ध.
—जरा-
भीरु, उस्, m. love or the deity Kāma (‘afraid of
old age’).
—जरा-मृत्यु, ऊ, m. du. old age and
death; (उस्, उस्, उ), one who dies from old age.
—जरा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, aged, old.
—जरावस्था
(˚रा-अव्˚), f. state of old age, decrepitude.
—जरा-
सन्ध, अस्, m., N. of a celebrated king and warrior,
sovereign of Magadha and Cedi, son of Bṛhad-ratha,
father-in-law to Kaṃśa, and enemy of Kṛṣṇa; he
was slain in single combat by Bhīma; (according to
a legend, he was born divided in two halves, which
were put together by the Rākṣasī Jarā, q. v.; he is
also identified with the Dānava Vipracitti, and men-
tioned among the hundred sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.)
—जरासन्ध-जित्, त्, m. ‘conqueror of Jarā-sandha,’
N. of Bhīma-sena, the second of the Pāṇḍu princes.
जर, जरथ, जरण, जरस्, &c. See p. 340.
1. जरा, f. old age &c. See under जर, col. 2.

2. जरा, f., Ved. crackling, roaring; invoking,
greeting; praise; [cf. 1. जरा above.]
—जरा-बोध,
अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. attending to invocation or praise.
—जराबोधीय, अम्, n., N. of several Sāmans.
जार जार, जारक, &c. See p. 350, col. 3.

जार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. becoming old; (अस्), m. a
paramour, gallant, lover, (in the Veda applied to Agni
or to the Sun as the paramour of the dawn); a
confidential friend; (ई), f. a particular herb or medi-
cament; a N. of Durgā; [cf. Goth. hôrs; Germ.
Hure.]
—जार-गर्भ, अस्, आ, अम्, pregnant by a
paramour.
—जार-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, a bastard, the child
of a woman by her paramour.
—जार-जात or जार-
जातक, अस्, आ, अम्, a bastard; (अस्), m. a plagiarist.
—जार-ता, f. an intrigue, love-affair.
—जार-द्वय,
अम्, n. a couple of gallants.
—जार-भरा, f. an
adulteress.

जरठ, अस्, आ, अम्, old, decayed, infirm; bent,
bowed down, drooping; hard, solid; hard-hearted,
harsh, cruel; pale, yellowish-white (the colour of old
leaves); (अस्), m. decrepitude, old age; [cf. Germ.
hart; Goth. hardus.]

जरण, अस्, आ, अम्, old, decayed, infirm; solvent,
promoting digestion; (अस्, अम्), m. n. several medi-
cinal plants or drugs used for promoting digestion, =
जीरक, cumin-seed; कृष्ण-जीरक, Nigella Indica;
= कास-मर्द and = कुष्ठौषधि; Asa Fœ-
tida; a sort of salt, Bit-lobon or Bit-lavana; (आ), f.
old age; the plant Nigella Indica; (अम्), n. old age,
becoming old and infirm; one of the ten ways in
which an eclipse is supposed to end.
—जरण-
द्रुम, अस्, m. the tree Vatica Robusta.
1. जरणा. See under जरण above.

जरणा 2. जरणा, f. (fr. 3. जॄ), Ved. roaring,
crackling, sounding; (Sāy.) invoking, praising; [cf.
1. जरण, col. 2.]
जरणा, जरितृ, जरूथ, &c. See s. v.

जारण, अम्, n. the act of causing to decay; pro-
moting digestion; calcining or oxidizing metals; a
condiment, a digester; (ई), f. a kind of cumin-seed.
जरण्ड, अस्, आ, अम्, decayed, old.
जरण्या, f., Ved. decrepitude.

जरत्, अन्, अन्ती (or अती ?), अत्, old, ancient, advanced
in years, infirm, decayed; (अन्), m. an old man; (ती),
f. an old woman; [cf. Gr. γέρων; Hib. gearait, ‘a
saint, a holy man;’ Germ. krank ?].
—जरत्-कारु,
उस्, उस्, m. f., N. of an ancient Ṛṣi of the family of
Yāyāvara, and of his wife who was a sister of the ser-
pent-prince Vāsuki, both being the parents of Āstīka;
(उस्), m. the Vyāsa of the twenty-seventh Dvāpara.
—जरत्कारु-प्रिया, f. the wife of Jarat-kāru exer-
cising a peculiar power over serpents, see the preceding.
—जरद्-अष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. reaching to a great
age, very old; (इस्), f. longevity.
—जरद्-गव, अस्,
m. an old bull or ox; N. of a vulture; (ई), f. an old
cow; [cf. गो-जर.]
—जरद्गव-वीथि, इस्, f. ‘the
course of the old bull,’ N. of a part of the moon's path
occupied by the constellations Vi-śākhā, Anu-rādhā,
and Jyeṣṭhā.
—जरद्-योषा, f. an old woman.
—ज-
रद्-विष्, ट्, ट्, ट्, Ved. (Sāy.) seizing on and devouring
dry (wood) or consuming water (applied to Agni).
जरतिका, f. an old woman.
जरतिन्, ई, m., N. of a man.
जरन्त, अस्, m. an old man; a buffalo.
जरयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, consuming, devouring.
जरयु, उस्, उस्, उ, becoming old; [cf. अ-जरयु.]

जरायु, उस्, उस्, उ, withering, dying away; (उ),
n. the slough or cast-off skin of a serpent; the
membrane which envelopes the fetus, the outer skin
of the embryo or chorion, (the inner or amnion is
called उल्व); after-birth, secundines; (उस्), m., N.
of a plant, = अग्नि-जार; also = जटायु; (उस्), f., N.
of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda; [cf.
ज्योतिर्-जरायु and निर्-जरायु.]
—जरायु-ज, अस्, आ,
अम्, born from the womb, viviparous, born alive.

जरस्, आ, f. (only जरस् before vowel-terminations,
Gram. 171), the becoming old, decay, decrepitude, old
[]
age; (आ), m., N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa by Turī; N. of
the hunter who wounded Kṛṣṇa; [cf. Gr. γῆρας.]

जरस at the end of an adv. comp. = जरस्; [cf.
आ-जरसम्.]
जरसान, अस्, m. a man.
जरायणि, इस्, m. = जरा-सन्ध.

जरित, अस्, आ, अम्, old, decayed; (आ), f., N. of a
Śārṅgikā (or kind of bird), the mother of four sons
at once by the Ṛṣi Manda-pāla in the form of a
male Sārṅgaka.
—जरितारि (˚त-अरि), इस्, m., N. of
the eldest son of Manda-pāla by Jaritā.

जरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, old, ancient, infirm, decayed; (ई),
m. an old man.

जरिमन्, आ, m., Ved. old age; decrepitude,
death from old age.

1. जरूथ, अम्, n. skinniness, flesh flaccid with
old age; flesh.

2. जरूथ, अस्, m., Ved. one who roars or makes
a noise; N. of a demon conquered by Agni; (Sāy.)
speaking harshly or to be invoked.

जर्जर, अस्, आ, अम्, old, infirm, decrepit, decayed;
torn or broken in pieces, split up into small particles,
divided in parts or pieces, broken; perforated,
wounded, hurt; dull, hollow (as the sound of a
broken vessel); (अम्), n. Indra's banner or emblem;
= सैवल, an aquatic plant.
—जर्जर-त्व, अम्, n.
the being old or decayed or perforated &c.
—जर्ज-
रानना (˚र-आन्˚), f., N. of one of the Mātṛs
attending on Skanda.
जर्जर जर्जर. See above.
जर्जरित, अस्, आ, अम्, torn in pieces, worn out.

जर्जरीक, अस्, आ, अम्, old, decayed; ragged,
perforated, full of holes.
जर्जरी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, wounded, disabled.

जर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, old, decayed; (अस्), m. the
(waning) moon; a tree.

जरडी जरडी, f. a kind of grass; [cf.
गर्मोटिका, जयाश्रया, सुनाला.]

जरणि-प्रा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. moving on with
noise; (Sāy.) increasing the wealth of the praiser.

जरणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be addressed with praise
or invoked.

जरण्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. invoking aloud; (Sāy.)
desiring praise.
जरमाण, अस्, m., N. of a man.

जरितृ, ता, m., Ved. an invoker, singer, praiser,
worshipper.

जर्च् जर्च्, cl. 1. 6. P. जर्चति, &c., to say,
speak; to reprove, abuse, blame; to
threaten.

जर्छ् जर्छ्, cl. 1. 6. P. जर्च्छति, &c., to
say, speak; to blame; [cf. चर्च्.]

जर्ज् जर्ज्, cl. 1. 6. P. जर्जति, &c., to say;
to blame, reprove; to kill or hurt (?).

जर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, torn to pieces, wounded;
(perhaps a wrong form for जर्जरित.)

जर्झ् जर्झ्, cl. 1. 6. P. जर्झति, to say or
speak; to blame; to threaten; [cf. जर्च्.]
जर्त जर्त, अस्, m. = जर्तु, q. v.
जर्तिक जर्तिक, आस्, m. pl. = बाहीक.

जार्तिक जार्तिक, आस्, m. pl. a various read-
ing for जर्तिक.
जर्तिल जर्तिल, अस्, m. wild sesamum.

जर्तु जर्तु, उस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. जन्),
the vulva; an elephant.

जर्त्स् जर्त्स्, cl. 1. P. जर्त्सति, &c., to say,
speak; to blame, censure, abuse; to
protect.

जर्भरि जर्भरि, इस्, इस्, इ (fr. rt. भृ ?), Ved.
supporting (?). According to Sāy. जर्भरी = भर्-
तारौ, supporters (epithet of the Aśvins).

जर्य जर्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. जॄ), becoming
old; [cf. अ-जर्य.]

जार्य जार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to
Sāy.) ‘to be praised’ (as if fr. 3. जॄ); but perhaps
rather (अम्), n. familiarity, intimacy, (fr. जार.)

जर्वर जर्वर, अस्, m., N. of a priest assist-
ing at a sacrifice by which the serpent-race overcame
death.

जर्हिल जर्हिल, अस्, m. wild sesamum; [cf.
जर्तिल.]
जारुधि जारुधि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain.

जारूथी जारूथी, f., N. of a river (?); [cf.
जरूथ.]

जारूथ्य जारूथ्य or जारुथ्य. This word
is generally found connected with अश्व-मेध, the
horse sacrifice, but the meaning is doubtful.

जारुत्थ, अस्, m. (is said to mean) a sacrifice in
which three offerings are made, or in which the sun
is thrice worshipped in his southern declination (?).
जार्यक जार्यक, अस्, m. a particular animal.

जारक, अस्, आ, अम्, causing to decay; promoting
digestion, digestive.

जारतिनेय, अस्, m. a metronymic from Jaratī; a
patronymic from Jaratin.

जारत्कारव, अस्, m. a patronymic from Jarat-
kāru.

जारद्गव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जरद्-गव), scil.
वीथि, the path of the old ox, (according to Varāha-
mihira the portion of the moon's path occupied by
the constellations Śravaṇā, Dhaniṣṭhā, and Śata-
bhiṣaj, or according to other authorities that occupied
by Vi-śākhā, Anu-rādhā, and Jyeṣṭhā.)
जारमाण्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Jaramāṇa.

जारासन्धि, इस्, m. (fr. जरा-सन्ध), a patro-
nymic of Saha-deva.

जारिणी, f., Ved. a woman who has a paramour,
enamoured.
जारुज, अस्, आ, अम्, = जरायु-ज.
